item.title: Librería de Satoshi Rebrands to ISMOS, Launches Global Platform to Train One Million Bitcoin Developers
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Librería de Satoshi Rebrands to ISMOS, Launches Global Platform to Train One Million Bitcoin Developers Librería de Satoshi, the technical education organization, recently announced the launch of its global platform as they rebrand to ISMOS and shows off a new website. The organization aims to expand its Bitcoin and open-source developer education program throughout the world, creating local hubs across the world and delivering education programs in local languages. Since 2021, ISMOS has reached more than 3,665 people in more than 40 countries and has financially supported 30 open-source developers, according to a press release shared with Bitcoin Magazine. “Talent is universal; opportunity is not. I founded Librería de Satoshi because I experienced the language barrier in Bitcoin firsthand. ISMOS takes that mission worldwide, so that the next great developer can come from anywhere,” said Dulce Villarreal, CEO and founder of ISMOS. What began as a Bitcoin school for Spanish speakers is today a technical education ecosystem and a complete training path for freedom technologies and open-source developers. ISMOS brings together educators and technology creators: a space to learn and teach with “Freedom Tech values, in more languages, more regions, and more disciplines, with a growing presence in universities, bootcamps, and programming communities.” ISMOS was born in Latin America as Librería de Satoshi and is now a global movement. One Million Bitcoin Developers Around the World ISMOS combines rigorous study programs, direct mentorship, and fellowships in Spanish, Portuguese, and English, and soon in more languages. Subjects will include Bitcoin, cryptography, cybersecurity, mathematics, AI, Nostr, open-source software, and open AI models. The platform is open source, and software developers can explore its open tools at github.com/ismos-xyz . Today ISMOS is primarily supported by Btrust and the Human Rights Foundation. Other organizations, such as OpenSats and the Gemini Opportunity Fund, have supported its work in the past with smaller grants, according to the press release. The announcement reflects nearly five years of growth and a deeper commitment to equal opportunity. “Someone coding in Argentina, Nigeria, or El Salvador deserves the same chance to build a first-class technical career as anyone in Silicon Valley or London.” SMOS aims to go beyond study programs to provide individual support to the best developers through programs such as B4OS (Bitcoin 4 Open Source), fellowships, and its developer residencies: “in their language, at their level, and with the specific support they need to go further than they imagined.” Press contact Karina Conde, Director of Operations. comms@ismos.xyz This post Librería de Satoshi Rebrands to ISMOS, Launches Global Platform to Train One Million Bitcoin Developers first appeared on Bitcoin Magazine and is written by Juan Galt .

item.title: Democrats to Target Trump’s Crypto Ventures After Taking Congress
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Democrats to Target Trump’s Crypto Ventures After Taking Congress House Democrats plan to open investigations into President Donald Trump’s family crypto businesses once they take control in January, with World Liberty Financial, its Emirati investor and the pardon of Binance founder Changpeng Zhao at the top of the list. Rep. Robert Garcia of California, who will chair the House Oversight Committee, answered the Associated Press call with a two-word statement at 3:18 a.m.: “Lawyer up.” His office said he intends to take on what it calls the “Trump Crime Family” alongside corporate corruption, immigration enforcement abuses and the Epstein files. Garcia told Punchbowl News the committee will examine the family’s crypto deals, Donald Trump Jr.’s business dealings and relatives such as Jared Kushner “sitting on boards and getting contracts.” The difference from the past two years is subpoena power. Democrats have written letters, requested Treasury probes and held shadow hearings; the majority lets them compel documents and testimony from the administration and from private companies without the president’s consent. Reuters reported in September that inquiries could begin as early as February, with corporate donors to the White House ballroom and firms that did deals with Trump relatives among the first targets. World Liberty Financial, the DeFi and stablecoin venture the Trump family launched in September 2024, is expected to come first. Democrats have focused on a $500 million investment by Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed Al Nahyan, the UAE national security adviser, whose vehicle took a reported 49% stake shortly before the January 2025 inauguration. The stake matters because World Liberty is seeking a federal trust bank charter for its USD1 stablecoin; the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted conditional approval on Aug. 14, with final sign-off pending. Tahnoon’s group and a Trump-affiliated entity together control about 87% of the bank’s holding company, according to The Wall Street Journal. House Democrats asked Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent in February to investigate the deal and sought suspicious activity reports tied to the family’s ventures. Those requests carried no legal force. Senate Democrats on the Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, led by Richard Blumenthal, opened their own inquiry into the TRUMP token and World Liberty earlier this year. The second target is the October 2025 pardon of Zhao, whose exchange helped launch USD1 and was hacked for $6.34 billion last week. Zhao has said he has no business ties to the Trump family and did not discuss clemency with them. Trump’s 2025 financial disclosure listed more than $1 billion in crypto-related income, including about $635 million in TRUMP memecoin royalties; Reuters put the family’s crypto earnings at $2.3 billion or more. item.title: TD Cowen: Democratic Sweep Makes a Crypto-Backed CLARITY Act ‘Impossible’
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine TD Cowen: Democratic Sweep Makes a Crypto-Backed CLARITY Act ‘Impossible’ The Democratic sweep of Congress closes the door on crypto market structure legislation like the Clarity Act for the next two years and may rule out any version the industry would support, TD Cowen told clients in a note published after the Associated Press called both chambers. “We view this outcome as negative for our sectors,” Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg wrote. The caveat he has repeated all cycle still holds: the election “will not impact the ability of regulators to push their de-regulatory agendas,” and he expects the SEC and CFTC “to remain active including on crypto, prediction markets and perps.” The items he flags to watch are the lame-duck session, congressional investigations of Trump, the debt ceiling and populist bills such as interest rate caps. The note lands after a bruising week for the industry: a record $6.34 billion Binance hack , the loss of House allies Bryan Steil, Zach Nunn and Ann Wagner, and more than $170 million in super PAC spending that failed to deliver the Congress it was meant to buy. Clarity, Brown and World Liberty Seiberg’s crypto calls build on a note he published Tuesday , before the results. Sherrod Brown’s return to the Senate from Ohio, after about $64 million in industry money went to stopping him, “damages the crypto industry’s political clout,” he wrote. He had not expected the CLARITY Act to pass in the next Congress; Brown’s win “makes us more confident in our prediction.” The bill, which passed the House in July 2025 and failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 in September, dies on Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it. Seiberg goes further than most: Democratic investigations of the Trump family’s crypto ventures, including World Liberty Financial, “may make it impossible to advance a version of Clarity that the crypto sector could back.” That shifts the question from timing to whether any bill the industry wants can pass under this Congress. The agencies are the counterweight. Seiberg sees no change at the SEC or CFTC, which have cleared bitcoin perpetuals , equity perps and a joint crypto taxonomy this year without Congress. The CME lawsuit over the perps approval is the live threat to that path, not the election. Debt ceiling, confirmations and the Fed The rest of the note reads as macro risk for an asset that has traded with the Nasdaq all autumn. Seiberg expects a push to raise the debt ceiling in the lame duck but doubts it succeeds, since Democrats will want the vote as leverage next year. Divided government raises the odds of a shutdown or default standoff in 2027. He sees Trump and Sen. Elizabeth Warren, the likely Senate Banking chair, finding common ground on an interest rate cap, closer to 36% than the 10% Trump has floated, with fintechs more exposed than banks. item.title: Riot (RIOT) and Hut 8 (HUT) Sell Thousands of Bitcoin to Fund AI Ventures, Share Buybacks
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Riot (RIOT) and Hut 8 (HUT) Sell Thousands of Bitcoin to Fund AI Ventures, Share Buybacks Two of the largest public bitcoin miners reported third-quarter results on Wednesday, and both used the occasion to confirm they have been selling the asset they were built to accumulate. Riot Platforms has sold 20,264 BTC this year for about $1.5 billion, and Hut 8 has sold 3,102 BTC since July to fund $250 million in share repurchases. The sales serve different ends. Riot is paying for data center construction; Hut 8 is buying back its own stock. Riot ended September with 2,418 BTC, worth about $202 million at the quarter-end price of $83,554. It held 18,005 at the start of the year. Hut 8 reported about 16,787 BTC across the parent and its majority-owned American Bitcoin on Sept. 30, worth $1.4 billion, of which $697.4 million was attributable to Hut 8 itself, before October sales reduced the parent’s share. Riot: the treasury becomes a construction budget Riot’s selling has been steady all year. It sold 3,778 bitcoin in the first quarter, about 2.5 times its production, then 4,300 in the second and a further 12,186 in the third. The proceeds funded data center work and the full repayment of a $200 million Coinbase credit facility, which released all pledged coins. The company raised no equity in 2026. The reason arrived with the results. Riot signed a 15-year triple-net lease with an unnamed “Frontier AI Lab” for the whole of its Corsicana, Texas campus, 910 MW of critical IT capacity, worth about $28 billion over the initial term and $1.8 billion in average annual rent. Combined with its AMD contract and an earlier Rockdale lease with the same tenant, Riot has leased 1,151 MW for about $38 billion. CEO Jason Les put expected net operating income above $2 billion a year at full deployment, according to the company release. The structure limits Riot’s outlay. Capital cost is about $6 million per MW, half a typical Tier 3 build; Riot funds $2 million of that for site work and power, and the tenant covers the rest, to be reimbursed from non-recourse project debt after each phase is delivered. Delivery runs from September 2027 to July 2028. Mining continues in the background. Riot produced 1,637 BTC in the quarter at an average cost of $39,265 before depreciation, but mining revenue fell 28% to $116 million as the average price dropped to $70,855 from $114,361 a year earlier. Total revenue was $181.4 million, flat year over year, with data center and engineering income filling the gap. Hut 8: bitcoin out, shares in Hut 8’s sales went to shareholders rather than contractors. It sold about 954 bitcoin for $74.8 million in the quarter and about 2,148 BTC for $175.4 million in October, retiring 3.3 million shares for a combined $250 million. On Nov. 2 the board raised the repurchase authorization to $1 billion. item.title: Circle (CRCL) Cuts About 5% of Workforce as Q3 Revenue Hits $865M
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Circle (CRCL) Cuts About 5% of Workforce as Q3 Revenue Hits $865M Circle Internet Group cut about 5% of its workforce in the third quarter, a reduction the USDC issuer disclosed in the footnotes of an earnings report that showed revenue rising 17% to $865 million and net income up 5% to $226 million. The company booked a $9.1 million restructuring charge for the cuts, which it described as “designed to better align our organizational structure with our operating model and strategic priorities.” The charge covered notice-period pay, severance and benefits. Circle did not say how many employees were affected or which teams were hit, and the layoffs did not appear in the release’s list of business highlights. CRCL shares slipped about 1.2% in premarket trading to $74.33 after gaining 4.4% on Tuesday. The stock trades at a fraction of the highs it reached after its June 2025 IPO. A token sale carried the quarter The headline growth masks a softer core. Reserve income, the interest Circle earns on the Treasuries and cash backing USDC, fell 8% from a year earlier to $658 million as the reserve return rate dropped 61 basis points to 3.5%. Average USDC in circulation grew 8% to $73.3 billion, not enough to offset lower yields, and circulation at quarter-end was flat year over year at $73.9 billion. Circle’s share of the fiat-backed stablecoin market slipped to 27%. What filled the gap was a one-time item. Other revenue jumped to $207 million from $29 million, with $182 million of that from the private presale of ARC, the token for Circle’s new Arc blockchain. Strip that out and total revenue would have declined. Adjusted EBITDA of $317 million, up 85%, carries the same presale. The cost side tells the rest. Operating expenses rose 16% to $245 million on higher general and administrative, depreciation, IT and marketing spending, while distribution costs, the fees Circle pays partners such as Coinbase to hold USDC, fell 8% to $409 million. The workforce cut lands as the company builds Arc, integrates a January asset acquisition and prepares to absorb Tazapay. Circle is spending on the next business Circle is paying for growth outside its core product. Arc’s public mainnet launched Sept. 16 with more than 100 institutional builders, and Circle minted the full 10 billion ARC supply, becoming the first public company to issue a network token for its own layer-one chain. It agreed to buy Tazapay, a Singapore cross-border payments platform with more than $25 billion in annualized volume, in a deal expected to close in 2027. Binance, days before its $6.34 billion hack , put $100 million into Circle equity and renewed a USDC distribution partnership. The GENIUS Act takes effect Jan. 18, bringing federal licensing and reserve rules for stablecoin issuers, a regime the Federal Reserve has begun to fill in. item.title: Bitcoin Price Soars Above $79,000 After Democratic Sweep of Congress
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Bitcoin Price Soars Above $79,000 After Democratic Sweep of Congress Bitcoin price traded near $79,200 on Wednesday morning, up about 2% on the day, after Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate in Tuesday’s midterm elections and dealt the crypto industry its worst night in Washington since 2022. The Associated Press called the Senate for Democrats late Tuesday and the House early Wednesday. House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries is in line to become speaker. The result exceeded most forecasts: by Wednesday morning the AP tracker showed Democrats with 54 Senate seats to Republicans’ 44, with races still open. Prediction markets had put a Democratic House above 90% for weeks, but the Senate margin and the loss of several Republican crypto allies in the House came as a surprise. The bitcoin price reacted in two moves. Bitcoin fell to $75,618, a seven-week low, as results came in during Asian trading, then recovered the full loss and more by the European open. Traders broadly speaking treated the sweep as the removal of a known risk rather than a shock: prediction markets had priced a Democratic win for weeks, and options desks saw heavy call buying on election day, with block volume more than double the prior session. The view on the desks is that a Democratic Congress is less friendly to crypto legislation but that divided government, a presidential veto and executive orders cap how much policy can change, leaving technical targets near $82,000 as the next test. Demand remains the weak point, with U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs shedding about $1.16 billion over three sessions and the price still about 27% below where it stood a year ago, down from about $80,500 a week before the vote. The races that cost bitcoin and crypto The industry’s super PACs spent more than $170 million this cycle, most of it for Republicans, and the headline bets failed. Sherrod Brown won back an Ohio Senate seat in a special election against Sen. Jon Husted despite about $64 million in crypto money aimed at stopping him, the largest sum the industry has spent against any single candidate. Brown chaired the Senate Banking Committee until his 2024 defeat and spent that tenure resisting market structure bills. Senate seniority rules may limit his path back to a gavel, but he returns to a chamber his party controls. Three House Republicans the industry counted on lost their seats: Bryan Steil of Wisconsin, who fell to ER nurse Mitchell Berman; Zach Nunn of Iowa; and Ann Wagner of Missouri. Stand With Crypto had endorsed Steil and Nunn and directed ad money to both. Mike Lawler of New York conceded to Democrat Cait Conley with the race uncalled. House Financial Services Chairman French Hill appears to have held his Arkansas seat but will hand the gavel to Rep. Maxine Waters. item.title: Tether Holds 150,000 Bitcoin CEO Says, 50,000 More Than Its Reserve Report Shows
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Tether Holds 150,000 Bitcoin CEO Says, 50,000 More Than Its Reserve Report Shows Tether holds about 150,000 bitcoin, worth some $11.5 billion at current prices, CEO Paolo Ardoino said, a figure that exceeds the holdings implied by the company’s latest reserve attestation by roughly 50,000 coins. “We have give or take 150,000 bitcoin ourselves. It’s not much, but it’s honest work,” Ardoino said during his keynote at the Plan ₿ Forum in Lugano, Switzerland, the city where Tether has run a bitcoin and stablecoin adoption program since 2022. At that size the stack would rank Tether among the largest corporate holders of bitcoin, behind Strategy’s 848,517 BTC ( as of Q3 ) and ahead of most public miners and treasury companies. Ardoino did not say where the additional coins sit, when they were bought or whether they belong to the stablecoin issuer or to Tether Investments, the arm that holds the group’s venture and equity positions. The remark does not indicate a new 50,000 BTC purchase. JUST IN: Tether now holds approximately 150,000 Bitcoin worth $11.5 billion, CEO Paolo Ardoino announces pic.twitter.com/s7HLmXwkQE — Bitcoin Magazine (@BitcoinMagazine) November 3, 2026 Tether International’s third-quarter reserve report, published Oct. 30 with an attestation from BDO, lists $8.37 billion in bitcoin valued at $83,621.23 per coin as of Sept. 30. That implies about 100,060 BTC, up around 1,130 from the roughly 98,930 held at the end of June. Most of the quarter’s $2.57 billion rise in the bitcoin line came from price, not purchases. The gap between the report and Ardoino’s figure has a plausible home. Tether has said the investments it makes from profits are kept apart from the reserves backing USDT, so coins held by Tether Investments would not appear in the attestation. Tether’s bitcoin exposure extends past its own wallets. It took full control of Twenty One Capital in May after buying out SoftBank, backs Adecoagro’s mining in Brazil, and runs mining and energy ventures in Latin America. Whether any of those positions sit inside the 150,000 figure is unclear. Tether’s buffer built on bitcoin and gold The disclosure lands as Tether’s balance sheet grows more dependent on the two assets. The Q3 report shows $191.45 billion in reserve assets against $183.50 billion in liabilities, an excess of $7.95 billion, up from $4.11 billion in June when the cushion had halved. Bitcoin at $8.37 billion and gold at about $19.1 billion together exceed that buffer several times over, so a sharp drop in either would eat into it. Treasury bills remain the bulk of reserves at about $132.4 billion. Tether earned about $1.5 billion in the quarter and $4.5 billion in the first nine months. In August it completed its first independent audit with KPMG, ending years of reliance on attestations alone. item.title: TD Cowen: Democratic Congress Would Sink CLARITY Act for Two Years
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine TD Cowen: Democratic Congress Would Sink CLARITY Act for Two Years A Democratic sweep of Congress would end the CLARITY Act’s chances for the next two years and sour the political climate for crypto, TD Cowen’s Washington analyst Jaret Seiberg wrote to Bitcoin Magazine and clients in an election-day note. Seiberg wrote that TD Cowen agrees with polls and prediction markets that Democrats are likely to take both chambers, with the caveat that polls taken a month out, which were more mixed, tend to beat those taken on the eve of a vote. His conclusion for crypto is blunt: “Democrats will likely investigate Trump including his crypto entanglements. We see this as souring the political environment for crypto, which is why we do not expect the Clarity Act to pass over the next two years.” The market structure bill passed the House 294-134 in July 2025 and failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15. If it does not pass before the new Congress convenes on Jan. 3, it dies and must be reintroduced. Seiberg added that crypto’s influence may shrink further in Congress if Sherrod Brown wins his Ohio Senate race, a contest the industry spent to lose. In Congress, the Senate is the lever The note treats Senate control as the bigger prize. A Democratic majority could block Trump’s nominees and use that power to force him to fill Democratic seats on the FDIC, SEC and CFTC, the three agencies at the center of crypto policy. It could pressure the White House to drop its effort to remove Lisa Cook from the Federal Reserve board. Trump could answer with acting chiefs, Seiberg wrote, but that risks handing authority to career staff, an outcome “Team Trump” does not want. Senate control would elevate Sen. Elizabeth Warren to chair the Banking Committee. Seiberg sees room for populist bills such as interest rate caps, limits on bank buybacks and a government credit score, and he thinks Warren and Trump could find common ground on some of them. Rep. Maxine Waters would take House Financial Services, with a focus on housing and tighter scrutiny of the FHFA. “That means a focus on housing though we are dubious that she will find GOP support for down payment help and public housing renovations. FHFA scrutiny will increase,” the note read. For banks, the note says the election changes little: regulators will keep easing capital, liquidity and tiering rules whichever party wins. Divided government does raise the odds of a shutdown or a debt-ceiling standoff, since Trump is expected to reject spending conditions Democrats attach. Bitcoin on election day Bitcoin traded near $77,500 Tuesday afternoon eastern time, up from a dip to $76,300 in the morning and about $2,000 below where it opened the month. The price has absorbed a record $6.34 billion Binance hack , two days of spot ETF outflows and a Fed that is leaning toward a December hike. item.title: Binance Says $6.34 Billion Hack Began With Fake Job Interview
item.description: Bitcoin Magazine Binance Says $6.34 Billion Hack Began With Fake Job Interview The $6.34 billion theft from Binance began with a fake job interview and ran for five months before a single coin moved, the exchange said Tuesday in its first public account of the Oct. 29 attack. Another initial incident report from Binance, released alongside a media briefing by co-CEO Richard Teng and chief security officer Jimmy Su, describes a campaign that combined a poisoned software download, a staged recruitment process, malware that evaded endpoint detection and an internal AI tool the attackers turned against the company’s own wallet engineers. Binance said it has frozen or intercepted about $2.85 billion of the stolen assets and replenished 98% of affected tokens from its own funds, with the balance being bought on the open market. “This wasn’t one mistake or one breach — it was a months-long campaign,” Teng wrote on X. “We’re publishing the full report because the lessons go far beyond Binance.” The FBI has attributed the attack to North Korea. Binance’s report cites that finding but stops short of its own attribution. Pyongyang rejected the claim Monday, with Kim Yo Jong, sister of leader Kim Jong Un, calling it a “grave political provocation” through state media. The Binance hack had five months of preparation According to Binance, the first foothold for this hack came in June. A wallet DevOps engineer searched for a popular AI coding tool and downloaded a tampered Homebrew installer. Binance’s security team caught the anomaly, replaced the device and rotated credentials, but the episode exposed the engineer’s role and the names of colleagues on the wallet infrastructure team. In September, a second engineer was approached on a legitimate job platform by someone posing as a project director. A video interview with a purported HR representative followed, with the interviewer sharing a personal social media account to build trust. A second interview with a supposed CEO ended with an “assignment”: a code repository the engineer was told to install on his work machine. The repository replaced a legitimate pyenv component with a malicious version and opened a channel to an attacker-controlled server. Binance said the zero-day malware was not flagged by its endpoint tools at the time. On Oct. 20, the attackers used that machine and an internal AI tool to reach two more wallet engineers, one of whom held a container deployment token. On Oct. 29, between 17:15 and 19:56 UTC, they logged into a third engineer’s computer, deployed a container with the stolen credentials and launched the drain. Binance said it blocked 57 other suspected North Korea-linked attempts this year using similar lures. Four hours to contain The money left fast. Between 20:05 and 20:09 UTC, five hot wallets sent 233.46 million XRP to an attacker address. Wallets on Solana and Optimism followed with about 970,500 SOL and 44.2 million OP. item.title: Andrew Hohns: Why Bitcoin Can Fix America’s Debt Spiral
item.description: ▶ Bitcoin Magazine Andrew Hohns: Why Bitcoin Can Fix America’s Debt Spiral U.S. federal debt has grown 40x in 45 years, from $1 trillion in 1981 to over $40 trillion. Andrew Hohns, founder and CEO of Battery Finance, explains why he doesn’t expect tax hikes or spending cuts to fix it, and how a strategic Bitcoin reserve could help defease the national debt. He also makes the case for the Treasury to pilot BitBonds.
